BiblicalUsage: Keruwb means a cherub, the winged figure of God's presence: Genesis 3:24 says God placed Cherubims at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword, to keep the way of the tree of life. Exodus 25:18 says thou shalt make two cherubims of gold, in the two ends of the mercy seat. 1 Chronicles 13:6 says the ark of God dwelleth between the cherubims. Psalms 99:1 says he sitteth between the cherubims, let the earth be moved.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the cherubim guard the way back to life and overshadow the mercy seat: the same wings that shut Eden open the way to atonement. I hold that the God who sits between the cherubim is not far off, and the earth should tremble because he reigns.
RelatedEvents: Creation; David Brings the Ark to Jerusalem
